title: Residual-Guided Multi-Resolution Refinement of Foundation Models: A Case Study in Drought Forecasting
claim: Experts analyze signals through staged multi-scale decomposition and error diagnosis, while single-pass black-box models miss complex patterns and leave large residual errors.
layout: 3 rows: raw series on top, expert steps middle, AI single-pass bottom; color-coded
description: A 3-row grid of line plots on SPEI (drought index) time series over 12 years. The top row is a wide plot of the raw series, with shaded bands marking seasonal patterns (blue), drought events (red) and multi-scale interactions (green). The middle row has three panels titled as Expert Steps 1–3. Step 1 shows broad annual patterns as a blue smoothed curve. Step 2 separates seasonal (green) from interannual (orange) oscillations. Step 3 shows purple residuals with red highlighted extreme events. The bottom row, in red, shows the AI single forward pass. The first panel has a 'BLACK BOX PROCESSING' label over the series. The second compares true SPEI with an AI prediction that misses patterns. The third plots prediction errors with large-error bands. The eye goes first to the colored titles and the shaded top plot.
caption: Comparison of temporal processing approaches in climate forecasting. Multi-scale decomposition analysis (middle row) versus single forward pass processing (bottom row) for complex climate pattern prediction.
abstract: Regional climate prediction presents unique challenges for time series foundation models, which typically process temporal patterns through single-pass inference. Expert climatologists, in contrast, employ multi-scale temporal analysis and iterative refinement based on systematic error diagnosis. We present RGMR (Residual-Guided Multi-Resolution Refinement), an inference-time framework that adapts pre-trained foundation models to perform structured coarse-to-fine refinement for climate forecasting without updating backbone parameters. Applied to drought forecasting using the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), RGMR is architecture-agnostic across the three TSFM backbones evaluated per site (TimesFM, TimeGPT, TabPFN) and consistently lowers test-set MSE on three South Australian sites and three additional regions outside South Australia. Applied to TimesFM, the wrapper reduces one-month-ahead SPEI MSE by up to 18.9\% across the three South Australian sites (mean reduction $\approx$18.7\%). Overall, RGMR provides a practical route for deploying frozen TSFMs in regional climate forecasting workflows.
